title: Saffy and the Sleepy Song
markdown:
Saffy had eyes as soft as the sky when it’s almost night, and her little legs were still a bit wobbly, just like little legs can be. She lived in a meadow. It was such a peaceful place! The moonbeams loved to play there. They would dance and whisper secrets to the sleepy flowers. The meadow always felt like a big, warm hug.

One night, Saffy was in her little bed made of clover. She was all snuggled and warm. But then, she felt a little bit sad. A tiny whisper of a worry tickled her nose. It felt as light as a feather. She couldn't remember a very special lullaby. It was a warm, sleepy tune. It made her eyelids feel heavy and her dreams feel sweet. It always made her feel safe and sound.

"Oh dear," Saffy thought. Her little ears drooped just a tiny bit. A small worry started to bloom in her heart.

Just then, a soft light glowed near her nose. It was Moth. Moth was a little lantern moth. Her wings sparkled like captured moonlight. She moved with a gentle flutter. Moth’s light was soft and warm. It wasn't a bright, startling light. It was like a tiny, friendly star that had come to visit. Her light glowed softly, like a quiet question. It seemed to ask, "What is wrong, little Saffy?"

"Hello, Moth," Saffy whispered. Her voice was as soft as leaves in a summer breeze. "I’ve forgotten my lullaby. The one that hums me to sleep."

Moth’s light glowed gently. It was like she understood. Moth drifted a little way into the moonlit garden. Her light was a steady glow that showed the path. Saffy’s wobbly legs felt steady in the cool air. She followed Moth. The moon made everything silver and soft blue. The garden looked like a peaceful dream. The flowers were sleeping under moonlight blankets.

They tiptoed past the tall reeds by the pond. The reeds swayed like dancers. They whispered and swayed. Saffy listened very closely. Their rustling sounded like soft voices. But it wasn't her lullaby.

"Hmm," Saffy sighed. A little puff of disappointment escaped her. Moth’s light blinked softly. It was a gentle, quiet nudge to keep going.

Moth then led Saffy to some moon-white flowers. Their petals felt like soft velvet. Moth hovered above. Her soft glow lit up a dewdrop. It was on a petal. The dewdrop was like a tiny mirror. It showed the big, round moon. It reflected all its gentle light.

Saffy looked into the dewdrop. She watched the moon shimmer. And then, a lovely, warm thought bloomed in her mind. It was like a flower opening to the sun. Her lullaby wasn't lost! It was just sleeping. It was tucked away inside her. Like the flowers sleeping peacefully under the moon. Waiting to be woken softly.

Moth seemed to understand. She guided Saffy closer to the sleeping flowers. Moth’s warm light seemed to ask the blossoms to sing. It whispered secrets of moonlight and rest. And then, something truly special happened. A sound, faint as a sigh on a warm evening, drifted from the flowers. It was a melody. It was so sweet and soft. It was so peaceful. It was like a whisper of dreams.

It was her lullaby! Saffy’s heart felt warm and full. It felt like a little nest ready for a sleepy bird. She hummed along. Her voice joined the gentle tune. Moth’s light glowed brighter than ever. It was a happy, warm pulse in the quiet night.

"Oh, thank you, Moth," Saffy whispered. A happy little yawn stretched her nose towards the moon. Moth’s light seemed to nod. Together, they went back to Saffy’s cozy clover bed. The lullaby was now a gentle song in Saffy’s heart. It was clear and comforting. She snuggled down. Her eyes felt heavy and warm. She pulled the clover leaves closer, like a soft blanket. The moonlight made soft patterns on the ground. Saffy felt perfectly safe and snug. She was wrapped in the quiet peace of the night. And soon, with the gentle light of Moth and the sweet, clear memory of her lullaby singing softly in her heart, Saffy drifted off to sleep. Her dreams were full of moonlit melodies. They were full of the quiet comfort of a true friend. Everything was just right.
characters: Saffy the fawn, Moth the lantern moth
